resultJson.description:
Each song's palette currently starts from `RGB.random`, so the lights have nothing to do with what's playing. Also, `PlaybackState` requires `item.album.images[0].url`, so a local file or a podcast episode makes every poll fail. This epic builds each song's base colour from its album cover. The base colour is the most vivid colour covering about 5% or more of the cover, found by the windowed hue-bin rule in ADR 0003. The palette of the configured type is built from that colour. Each cover's result is remembered by URL. A new light-show setting, `light-show.album-cover-colours`, turns this on or off. It defaults to true and is editable on the settings page next to the palette choice. Like the other settings, a change takes effect at the next song.

The design is fixed by `docs/adr/0003-take-each-song-s-base-colour-from-its-album-cover.md`, which is the source of truth for names, signatures, constants, log messages and error types. There is a pure part: `CoverColour.base` and `Palette.from(base, type)`, with `Palette.random` redefined through `from` so seeded palettes don't change. There is an I/O part: `client.AlbumCovers.fromHttp` with the sealed `client.CoverError`. Then the engine is wired up. `TrackShow` gains `base: RGB`. `showFor(trackId, cover)` runs the tempo lookup alongside a cover lookup capped at `SyncEngine.CoverWait = 1.second`. On timeout, or if `showFor` itself is cancelled, the cover fiber is cancelled in the background. Any timeout or failure gives a random base and exactly one WARN for that song. The show is fixed for the whole track, even if the cover arrives late. `applyNow` rebuilds a changed palette type from `show.base`. When the setting is off, when there is no cover URL, or when the cover has no vivid colour, the base is `RGB.random(using random)` exactly as today, with no WARN.

Three deliberate departures from the ADR:
1. **No SettingsPage DOM test.** The ADR asks for a SettingsPage test that toggles the checkbox. The `ui` tests run in plain Node.js with no DOM (no jsdom jsEnv is configured in `project/plugins.sbt`), so Laminar can't be mounted. The settings-page part of criterion 11 is shown by SectionsSpec instead: it checks that the key is on the page exactly once and right after `palette` in "All lights". The "takes effect at the next song" part is shown by an engine test that uses `LiveSettings.update`.
2. **`Async[F].both` instead of `parTupled`.** `showFor` uses `Async[F].both(tempo, coverBase)` rather than the ADR's `parTupled`. It is equivalent and needs no `Parallel` instance import.
3. **Cancelling the cover fiber.** The ADR has `coverBase` cancel the fiber only in its timeout fallback. The plan instead attaches `onCancel(fiber.cancel.start.void)` to the join, so the fiber is also cancelled if `showFor` is interrupted, for example at shutdown.

Documentation criteria (how-it-works, roadmap, architecture) are met by editing the docs; no test reads docs.

tasks.title: Make the album cover optional in PlaybackState
tasks.description:
Change `domain.spotify.PlaybackState.albumCoverUrl` from `String` to `Option[String]`, with the ADR's scaladoc line. In the decoder, compute it as `item.downField("album").downField("images").downArray.downField("url").focus.flatMap(_.asString)`. This is a plain Option, outside the Either for-comprehension (or lifted into it with `Right(...)`). Don't use `.as[Option[String]]`: circe's Option decoder returns Left when the cursor failed with an incorrect focus, which is what happens for `album: null` or `images: null`. tasks.title: Pure cover colour rule (CoverColour)
tasks.description:
Create `src/main/scala/domain/engine/CoverColour.scala` as sketched in the ADR's program design.
- Constants: `MinShare = 0.05`, `MinSaturation = 0.35`, `MinBrightness = 0.25`, `HueBins = 36`, `WindowBins = 1`.
- `isVivid`: saturation ≥ MinSaturation and brightness ≥ MinBrightness.
- `vividness`: saturation × brightness.
- `hueBin`: `floor(hue × HueBins)` mod HueBins, using `c.hsb`.
- `base(pixels: Seq[RGB]): Option[RGB]`.

The rule:
- For each of the 36 bins k, the window is bins k−WindowBins..k+WindowBins, taken mod 36.
- A window qualifies when its vivid pixels make up at least MinShare of all pixels. Neutral pixels count only towards the total.
- Among qualifying windows, the highest mean vividness wins, with a larger share breaking ties.
- The result has the window's circular-mean hue (average of unit vectors, atan2, normalised to [0, 1) turns) and its mean saturation and brightness. Build it via `Hsb.toRgb` and then `RGB.safe(r, g, b)`, which can't fail here; `RGB.fromHsb` is private.
- Empty input gives None.

Keep it pure: no randomness or I/O, and no `null` or `return`.

Tests: new `src/test/scala/domain/engine/CoverColourSpec.scala` (ScalaCheckSuite), with a small helper that builds RGB pixels from hue/sat/brightness via `Hsb.toRgb`.

Table, each row a synthetic pixel vector:
- mostly vivid red gives a base within ~10° of 0°
- mostly vivid blue gives blue
- all black, white and grey gives None
- neutral plus 4% vivid gives None
- neutral plus 6% vivid gives that hue
- a 6% red patch split between 356° and 4° gives red
- a 6% patch split between 28° and 32° gives a base within 10° of 30°
- separate 10% patches at 0° and 120° give one of those hues, not a blend near 60°

Properties:
- All-neutral input gives None.
- Whenever the result is Some, there is a bin k such that the vivid pixels with `hueBin` in k−1..k+1 (mod 36) make up ≥ MinShare of all pixels, and the result's hue lies in that window's 30° span, with a degree of rounding tolerance. Don't assert ±15° round the mean hue: the mean can sit off-centre, so that property is false.
- Rotation: generate one vivid cluster, all within ±3° of a bin centre and well inside the saturation and brightness thresholds, plus neutral filler. Rotating every pixel's hue by a multiple of 10° rotates the base hue by the same amount, within a few degrees.

tasks.title: Fetch and read album covers (AlbumCovers, CoverError)
tasks.description:
Create `src/main/scala/client/CoverError.scala` and `src/main/scala/client/AlbumCovers.scala` as in the ADR's program design. `CoverError.reason` gives "refused", "unreachable", "unreadable" or "timed_out".

`AlbumCovers.none[F: Applicative]` always gives `pure(None)`.

`AlbumCovers.pixels[F: Sync](url, bytes)`:
- Decodes inside `Sync[F].interruptible` with `Option(ImageIO.read(new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes)))`; scalafix forbids `null`.
- A null result, a thrown exception or a 0-sized image raises `CoverError.Unreadable(url)`.
- Samples down by stride to at most `MaxSide = 64` on each side, reading `img.getRGB(x * w / tw, y * h / th)` and masking out the r, g and b bytes.
- Returns `Vector[RGB]`.

`fromHttp[F: Async](client)` holds a `Ref[F, Map[String, Option[RGB]]]`. Its `baseColour(url)`:
- On a cache hit, including a cached None, returns the cached value with no request.
- Otherwise parses the URI. A parse failure becomes `Unreachable(url, err)`.
- GETs the URL with no credentials. A non-2xx response raises `Refused(url, status)`.
- Reads the body to bytes, then runs `pixels`, then `CoverColour.base`.
- Caches the result, including None, and logs DEBUG with `cover_url`, `base` (hex or "none") and `pixels` (the count).
- Turns any non-`CoverError` non-fatal throwable from the request or body into `Unreachable(url, err)`, and passes `CoverError`s through unwrapped.
- Doesn't cache failures and never logs image bytes.

Tests: new `src/test/scala/client/AlbumCoversSpec.scala` (CatsEffectSuite), plus a helper `src/test/scala/testkit/Covers.scala` that builds PNG bytes from (colour, share) stripes with `BufferedImage(TYPE_INT_RGB)` and `ImageIO.write(img, "png", baos)`. The engine task reuses this helper.

Use `Client.fromHttpApp` with routes serving:
- a mostly red PNG and a mostly blue PNG
- an all-grey PNG
- 404 and 500 responses
- garbage bytes
- a route that raises `new java.net.ConnectException`

Assert:
- red and blue give the right hue
- grey gives None
- 404 and 500 give `Refused` with that status
- garbage gives `Unreadable`
- the connect error gives `Unreachable`
- each case's `reason`, including `TimedOut`'s

With a request-counting `Ref`, show that a repeat call for the same URL makes no request, including after a None result, and that a failed URL is requested again on the next call. Test `pixels` directly: a 200×100 image yields at most 64×64 pixels, garbage raises Unreadable, and `none` gives None.

tasks.title: Take the base colour from the album cover in the engine, and wire it in Main
tasks.description:
Implement the rest of the ADR's SyncEngine diff.

Construction:
- The private constructor gains `covers: AlbumCovers[F]`.
- `SyncEngine.make` gains `covers: Option[AlbumCovers[F]] = None` as its last parameter and resolves `covers.getOrElse(AlbumCovers.none[F])` in the body. A default argument can't see the `Async` bound.
- The companion gets `val CoverWait: FiniteDuration = 1.second`.

`showFor(trackId: TrackId, cover: Option[String] = None)`:
- Runs the tempo lookup (error handling unchanged) and `coverBase(trackId, cover, settings)` with `Async[F].both`.
- The base is the cover's colour, or else `randomBase`.
- Builds the palette with `paletteFrom` and stores `TrackShow(..., base)`.
- Extends the INFO "New show for …" line with "base #rrggbb from the album cover" or "random base #rrggbb".

`coverBase`:
- With `!settings.albumCoverColours` or `cover` None, it gives `pure(None)` with no lookup and no log.
- Otherwise: `covers.baseColour(url).start.flatMap(fiber => fiber.joinWithNever.onCancel(fiber.cancel.start.void).timeoutTo(CoverWait, raiseError(CoverError.TimedOut(url, CoverWait))))`. The timeout cancels the join, and so does cancelling `showFor`; either way `onCancel` cancels the fiber in the background without waiting for it.
- Any `CoverError`, or other non-fatal throwable, becomes None with exactly one WARN: "Couldn't take the colours from the album cover for $trackId, using a random palette: ${err.getMessage}".
- The WARN uses structured context via `logger.warn(ctx)(msg)`: `track_id`, `cover_url` and `reason` (the `CoverError.reason`, or "failed"), plus `status` for Refused and `waited_ms` for TimedOut.
- `Right(None)` (no vivid colour) gives a random base and no WARN.

`playingFrame` calls `showFor(local.state.trackId, local.state.albumCoverUrl)`.

In `src/main/scala/Main.scala`, add `covers <- Resource.eval(AlbumCovers.fromHttp[IO](clients.spotify))` and pass `covers = Some(covers)` to `SyncEngine.make`. `ShowControls.palette` and `/api/palette` stay unchanged.

Tests: new `src/test/scala/SyncEngineCoverSpec.scala` (CatsEffectSuite, `TestControl.executeEmbed`, seeded Random), modelled on `SyncEngineRunSpec`'s `engine` and `alongside` helpers.

Setup:
- The fake Spotify's player JSON gives each track a cover URL, e.g. `https://covers.test/red`.
- Covers come from `AlbumCovers.fromHttp` over `Client.fromHttpApp`, with a request-counting Ref, serving: a red PNG, a blue PNG, an almost-grey PNG with a <5% vivid patch, a 500, garbage bytes, a raised `ConnectException`, and a slow red PNG behind `IO.sleep(2.seconds)`. Reuse `testkit.Covers`.
- For the late-cover test, wrap the covers in a test decorator `url => real.baseColour(url).uncancelable`. The fetch then really completes at 2 s and lands in the cache despite the background cancel.
- Capture logs with `testkit.Tls.capturedLogs` and `Tls.logged`, wrapped round the TestControl run. Count WARN events from logger `SyncEngine` whose message contains the track id.

Assert:
- **Red and blue covers (criteria 1 and 4).** A red cover gives a `show.base` with a red hue and `e.palette == Some(Palette.from(show.base, type).get)`. A blue cover gives blue. Also serve `SettingsRoutes` `/api/palette` with a `ShowControls` backed by `e.palette` and check that the hex list equals the cover palette.
- **Mostly neutral cover (criterion 2).** The base equals `RGB.random(using new Random(seed))`, and there is no WARN.
- **Failed covers (criterion 5).** A 500, an unreachable host and garbage bytes each give a random base and exactly one WARN for that song.
- **Late cover (criterion 6).** The slow, uncancelable cover gives a random base and one WARN with reason timed_out. The first playing frame comes within 1 s of the first poll. At 5 s the show's base and palette are still the random ones, even though the cover has arrived by then. A second track with the same URL then gets the red base with no new request.
- **Cache (criterion 7).** Two tracks with the same cover URL get the same cover-derived base, and the cover server sees one request.
- **No album (criterion 8).** No cover request, a random base and no WARN.
- **Apply now (criterion 9).** After a cover-derived base, `applyNow` with a new palette type gives `Palette.from(base, newType)`.
- **Setting off (criterion 10).** With `albumCoverColours = false`, there is no cover request and the palette equals `Palette.random(type)(using new Random(seed))`.
- **Mid-song change (criterion 11).** `live.update(albumCoverColours = false)` during track-1 keeps track-1's show, and track-2 makes no cover request.

tasks.description:
Docs only; no tests.

In `docs/how-it-works.md`:

resultJson.brief:
**Repo layout.** /work/spotify-hue-sync is Scala 3.9 built with sbt, in three modules:
- `root` (`.`): the app.
- `model/`: a crossProject (JVM + Scala.js) holding `LightShowConfig`, `RGB`, `Hsb`, `PaletteType`, `ConfigSnippet` and `SettingsView`.
- `ui/`: the Scala.js + Laminar settings page, tested with munit in plain Node.js. There's no DOM or jsdom, so only pure objects such as `Sections` and `Control` can be tested.

**Design source.** `docs/adr/0003-take-each-song-s-base-colour-from-its-album-cover.md` is the source of truth. Read its Program design, Failure modes and Observability sections. The epic description lists the plan's three deliberate deviations from it.

**CLAUDE.md rules.**
- Brace syntax for new code; `given`/`using`, not `implicit`.
- Cats Effect only (`F[_]: Async`, `Ref`, `Resource`): no Future, threads or unsafeRun.
- Errors are typed. Colour code stays pure. Make the smallest change; don't reshape working code. Comment only what the code can't say.
- Tests have no explanatory comments; the names say what they check. No test reads docs or README.
- Run `sbt fix`, then `sbt check`: lint, tests and coverage, with at least 90% of statements and 85% of branches overall and 70% of statements per file. Main, audio.AudioCapture, client.DtlsEmitter and beat.BeatTracking are excluded from coverage. Don't lower the minimums or disable rules.
- Never print, log or commit `.env`.

**Scalafix.** `.scalafix.conf` covers main code; tests use `.scalafix.test.conf`.
- DisableSyntax forbids `null` literals (wrap Java nulls in `Option(...)`), `return`, `isInstanceOf`, `implicitly`, `case true/false`, and unsafeRun or the global runtime.
- Other rules include ThrowableToNonFatal, DirectoryAndPackageName (the path must match the package), FileNameConsistent, ObjectFinal and DubiousLiteral.

**Key existing code.**
- `src/main/scala/SyncEngine.scala`: root package, with a colon-indented class body; keep it that way.
  - `case class TrackShow(tempo: Option[Double], palette: Palette, settings: LightShowConfig, zone: Zone)`, with `bpm`.
  - `class SyncEngine[F[_]: Async] private (config, live: LiveSettings[F], zone, spotify: SpotifyClient[F], lights: Lights[F], current: Ref[F, Option[(TrackId, TrackShow)]], random: Random, audio: Stream[F, AudioReading])`.
  - `private def newPalette(t): F[Palette]` (`Palette.random` using `random`), and `zoneFor`.
  - `def showFor(trackId): F[TrackShow]`. For a new track it runs `live.startSong`, then `getTempo` (a TLS failure logs ERROR, anything else WARN, and both give None), then the palette, the zone, `current.set`, and the INFO line \"New show for …\".
  - `def palette: F[Option[Palette]]`, and `def applyNow`, which keeps the palette unless its type changed.
  - `run` merges a poller and a renderer. The poller is `awakeEvery(pollingIntervalMs)` → `spotify.getPlaybackState` → a `SignallingRef`. The renderer is `awakeEvery(frameIntervalMs)` → `playingFrame` → `showFor(local.state.trackId)`.
  - Companion: `make(config, live, spotify, zone, lights, random = new Random(), audio = Stream.empty)`.
  - Logger: `Slf4jLogger.getLogger[F]`, a `SelfAwareStructuredLogger` with `warn(ctx: Map[String, String])(msg)`. Its name is `SyncEngine`.
- `src/main/scala/domain/engine/Palette.scala`: `case class Palette(colors: Vector[RGB])`. `random(mode)(using rnd: Random = Random): Option[Palette]` makes one `RGB.random` draw. Extensions: `getColor` and `along`.
- `model/src/main/scala/domain/engine/RGB.scala`:
  - `RGB(r, g, b: ByteInt)`, refined to 0–255.
  - `RGB.safe(r, g, b): Option[RGB]`, and `RGB.random(using Random): Option[RGB]`, which makes three `nextInt(256)` calls.
  - Extensions: `compliment`, `analogous` (−30°, base, +30°), `monochromatic` (brightness 0.35/0.65/1.0), `triadic`, `tetradic`, `hsb: Array[Float]` (h, s, b in 0..1), `hex`, `rotateHue(Int)`, `withBrightness` and `turnTowards`. `fromHsb` is private.
- `model/.../Hsb.scala`: `Hsb.fromRgb(r, g, b): Array[Float]` and `Hsb.toRgb(h, s, b: Float): (Int, Int, Int)`. Both match `java.awt.Color`.
- `src/main/scala/domain/spotify/PlaybackState.scala`: `PlaybackState(trackId, progress, isPlaying, albumCoverUrl: String)`, with a hand-written circe Decoder that requires the cover today. Only `PlaybackStateSpec` reads the field. `SpotifyClient` and some specs import the type but never touch the field.
  - Circe gotcha: `.as[Option[String]]` on a cursor that failed with an incorrect focus (`downField` on a JSON null, or `downArray` on null) gives Left, not None. Use `.focus.flatMap(_.asString)`.
- `model/src/main/scala/domain/config/LightShowConfig.scala`: a case class with defaults, `derives Codec.AsObject`. Missing fields fail to decode, which is fine because one build ships both the page and the server. `problems` and `validate` are in the companion.
  - `src/main/scala/domain/config/LightShowConfigReaders.scala`: `ConfigReader.derived[LightShowConfig].emap(validate)`.
  - Defaults are also in `src/main/resources/reference.conf` (the `light-show { … }` block), and `LightShowConfigSpec` asserts they equal the case-class defaults.
  - `ConfigSnippet.paths/changes/of` derive kebab-case paths from field names (`albumCoverColours` → `album-cover-colours`).
- UI files:
  - `ui/src/main/scala/ui/Control.scala`: an enum of the non-slider controls, with their `keys`.
  - `ui/src/main/scala/ui/Sections.scala`: `allLights` at ~line 235 has `controls = List(Control.Palette, Control.SongPalette, Control.RestingColour)`; `all` is at line 347.
  - `ui/src/main/scala/ui/SettingsPage.scala`: the `control(c)` match is at ~line 107; `reactionsSwitch` (~line 146) is the checkbox pattern; `paletteChoice` is at ~line 182; helpers are `edit(change)` and `marked(key)`.
  - `ui/src/test/scala/ui/SectionsSpec.scala`: 'every setting is on the page exactly once' compares the control and slider keys with `ConfigSnippet.paths(defaults)`. A model field with no UI control breaks it.
- `src/main/scala/Main.scala`: wires `HttpClients.resource`. `clients.spotify` is an Ember client with system TLS and FollowRedirect(2), and no auth; SpotifyClient adds tokens itself. Then it calls `SyncEngine.make[IO](…, audio = audio)`. `controls(engine, lights)` builds the `ShowControls`; its `palette` is `engine.palette.map(_.fold(Vector.empty)(_.colors))`, which `/api/palette` (`settings/SettingsRoutes.scala`) serves.
- `src/main/scala/client/`: the http4s clients and their error types. New `CoverError.scala` and `AlbumCovers.scala` go here, in package `client`.

**Testing.**
- munit 1.0, `munit.ScalaCheckSuite`, `munit.CatsEffectSuite`, and `cats.effect.testkit.TestControl.executeEmbed` for anything timed. Tests are forked and run sequentially.
- `src/test/scala/SyncEngineRunSpec.scala` is the template for engine tests.
  - The fake Spotify uses `HttpRoutes.of[IO]`:
    - `GET /v1/me/player` answers `{ progress_ms, is_playing, item: { id, album: { images: [ { url } ] } } }`.
    - `GET /v1/audio-features/:id` answers `{ \"tempo\": 128.0 }`.
  - It builds `new SpotifyClient[IO](Client.fromHttpApp(app), SpotifyCredentials(\"id\",\"secret\",Some(\"refresh\")), sessionRef(Some(SpotifySession(\"token\",\"refresh\"))), Deferred[IO,String])`, then `LiveSettings.make[IO](show)` and `SyncEngine.make[IO](config(show), live, spotify, zone, lights, new Random(seed), audio)`.
  - Helpers: `run(setup, duration)` and `alongside(setup, duration)((engine, live) => IO[A])`.
  - `pollingIntervalMs = 1000`, so the first poll is at 1 s of simulated time.
  - 'uses the configured palette type' asserts `show.palette == Palette.random(Tetradic)(using new Random(42L)).get`, so a random base must stay a single `RGB.random` draw.
- Log capture:
  - `testkit.Tls.capturedLogs: Resource[IO, ListAppender[ILoggingEvent]]` attaches to the root logger, and `Tls.logged(appender)` lists the events.
  - Filter on `getLevel == Level.WARN`, `getLoggerName == \"SyncEngine\"` and `getFormattedMessage`. The root level in the test logback config is WARN.
  - `SyncEngineLogSpec` doesn't capture logs, despite what the ADR says.
- `testkit.Colours`: the `rgb` and `vivid` Gens, `hue/saturation/brightness(c)`, `hueDistance(a, b)` in turns, `degrees`, and `close(a, b, tol)`.
- `testkit.Settings.valid` builds `LightShowConfig` positionally at line ~42, and `SettingsJsonSpec` round-trips it.
- In-memory PNGs: `java.awt.image.BufferedImage(w, h, TYPE_INT_RGB)`, `setRGB`, then `ImageIO.write(img, \"png\", ByteArrayOutputStream)`.
- `Client.fromHttpApp` ignores the host, so match routes on the path: `https://covers.test/red` matches `GET -> Root / \"red\"`.
- Under TestControl, `IO.sleep` in a route runs on simulated time. Background cancellation stops a route mid-sleep, so a test that needs a late cover to really finish wraps the lookup in `.uncancelable`.

**Concurrency.**
- `showFor` uses `Async[F].both`.
- Use `fiber.joinWithNever` so the cover's errors propagate.
- Attach `.onCancel(fiber.cancel.start.void)` to the join, before `timeoutTo`. Both the timeout and an outer cancellation then cancel the fiber in the background without waiting for it.

**Docs.**
- `docs/how-it-works.md`: section 3 → '### Palettes' at ~line 108, the config table in section 7 at ~line 317, and the settings page in section 8 at ~line 350.
- `docs/roadmap.md`: the album-cover item is at line 12.
- `docs/architecture.md`: the package table and the mermaid component and class diagrams.
